title: Delay Replacing a Missing Tooth: Risks, Costs, Next Steps
seoTitle: What Happens If You Delay Replacing a Missing Tooth
seoDescription: Bone loss, shifting teeth and bigger bills follow an untreated gap. See the timeline and your options, then plan early with our Santa Clarita team.
excerpt: A gap does not stay still. Bone shrinks, neighbors tip and the fix gets bigger. Here is how fast it happens and what to do now.
keyTakeaways: Bone in the socket starts to resorb soon after a tooth is lost, and neighboring teeth begin to drift.
Within 3 to 12 months, an implant may already require grafting or orthodontic space reopening.
Delay can turn a single implant into staged surgery, grafts or multiple restorations at higher cost.
Partials, flippers or a bonded bridge can hold the space while you plan a definitive replacement.
An exam with CBCT imaging is the reliable way to know how much bone remains and which options are open.
